races.name: Total Task Consultancy Prosperity Apprentice Handicap

runners_data.name: Shes Got The Blues
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins on good ground over 7f, stepping up to 1m here for the first time — the extra distance is the key question, but her form trajectory is strong and apprentice Myla Coppins claims 3lb; natural hold-up horse with the best recent profile in this field.
runners_data.comment: Took a Brighton classified race by three lengths last time, continuing to improve as her record advances; effective up to a mile on any going and in good heart, she arrives off a competitive mark and rates a clear danger.

runners_data.name: My Old Mate
runners_data.note: Struggled in eight straight starts without a win and carries a stamina concern with a noted tendency to fade in the finish — Jude Fernandes rides for a yard in reasonable form (T14: 4/28) but the finishing-line evidence makes this horse hard to trust in a race likely decided by a sharp sprint.
runners_data.comment: Beaten a head at this course and distance last time on a mark just 1lb below today's, showing a return to something approaching his better form; effective at a mile on any ground, he has an each-way chance on that evidence.

runners_data.name: Buckland Belle
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance on good going (1/8f/GOO), which is the most relevant piece of form in the race; although her natural style places her at the back, she is pushed into midfield on the map because the field is full of hold-up horses — her Windsor course form is the standout positive.
runners_data.comment: Keen to post but still finished half a length off in third on an unchanged mark last time; stays a mile on any going and has been in decent form — she remains competitive at this level and should go close again.

runners_data.name: Labiche
runners_data.note: Henry Candy's filly has shown flashes of ability (third on two of her last four starts) but has not run on good-to-firm ground before and her headgear (p) suggests she needs visual encouragement; a true backmarker whose chance is tempered by being placed into a midfield role she may not be comfortable settling in.
runners_data.comment: His peak effort to date came at Wolverhampton last time, beaten four lengths off a mark just a pound above today's; first-time cheekpieces on fast ground suits his preferences, and with a fair mark, he has claims despite being yet to score.

runners_data.name: She's Crafty
runners_data.note: A second over 7f on good ground (2/7f/GOO) is her best effort and suggests she handles the conditions, but her record over 8f is moderate and she has been pushed out of her natural rearward position into the mapped midfield — Alexandra Egan's 3lb claim is useful, but style-fit discount applies.
runners_data.comment: Well beaten at Leicester most recently on fast ground that arguably does not suit her at her best; handles today's trip on softer going and the mark is not unfair, but a consistent tendency to fall short of her best makes her hard to trust.

runners_data.name: Lapidarist
runners_data.note: David Simcock sends out a horse returning from a 95-day absence, the longest layoff in the field, which is a meaningful fitness concern; genuinely stays further than today's mile based on her second over 10f, but her true hold-up style being mapped to midfield and the long break make her a significant risk to trust.
runners_data.comment: Off a short break and returning for a trainer currently in good form, she was beaten close to seven lengths at Wolverhampton last time when the trip looked too short; ideally needs ten furlongs on artificial surfaces, and today's conditions do not play to her strengths.

races.paceDynamic: With no confirmed front-runner in a six-runner field, this 1m Windsor contest is likely to begin steadily before developing into a sprint finish in the straight, with no horse willing to sacrifice herself at the head of affairs. Shes Got The Blues, despite her hold-up tag, is the only runner showing recent winning form and brings the strongest in-running profile on similar going, giving her a meaningful edge in a race likely to be decided in the final two furlongs. My Old Mate carries a concerning tendency to fade in the finish, which is a significant liability in a race that may not test stamina early but will demand a sharp late effort. The field is loaded with hold-up types — Buckland Belle, Labiche, She's Crafty, and Lapidarist are all natural backmarkers redistributed to midfield on the map because there are simply more closers than the race can accommodate, meaning none of them is guaranteed their preferred racing position; Shes Got The Blues, with her recent course-relevant form and OK going tag, is best placed to benefit from this compressed, sprint-finish shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow-Run Sprint Finish
scenarios.trigger: If the pace remains pedestrian throughout and the race ignites only inside the final 2f, turning into a dash for the line.
scenarios.body: If the pace remains pedestrian throughout and the race ignites only inside the final 2f, turning into a dash for the line.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Positional Scrap Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If several hold-up types push forward to avoid cover, creating unexpected mid-race jostling and a more strung-out shape than anticipated.
scenarios.body: If several hold-up types push forward to avoid cover, creating unexpected mid-race jostling and a more strung-out shape than anticipated.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Farther Back Runners Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the race develops enough early tempo that the genuine backmarkers get a true end-to-end test that stretches the field.
scenarios.body: If the race develops enough early tempo that the genuine backmarkers get a true end-to-end test that stretches the field.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Two Pull Clear
scenarios.trigger: If one or two runners press forward aggressively from the outset and set a strong enough gallop to sap the closers' finishing kicks.
scenarios.body: If one or two runners press forward aggressively from the outset and set a strong enough gallop to sap the closers' finishing kicks.

watchPoints.text: Buckland Belle is the only runner with a proven win at this course and distance on comparable going — watch whether Conor Whiteley can manoeuvre her into a position that resembles her natural backmarker run despite being surrounded by hold-up rivals.

My Old Mate's tendency to fade in the finish is a red flag in a race that is likely to be run at a modest early pace and then explode late — if the final 2f become a sprint, her chance may evaporate quickly.
Lapidarist returns from 95 days off for a yard showing minimal recent activity (T14: 0/2) — monitor market moves and early show of condition in the paddock before drawing conclusions.

With no natural front-runner confirmed, watch which jockey breaks quickest from the stalls — any rider who pushes forward unexpectedly from the outside draws could reshape the entire race dynamic and catch the backmarkers flat-footed.

Shes Got The Blues arrives on a six-day turnaround having won twice at 7f on good ground — the step to 1m is untested and worth monitoring in running to see if she travels with the same fluency she showed over the shorter trip.

races.name: Sporting Life Sri Lanka Restricted Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Seathegulls
runners_data.note: Prominent racer for Gary & Josh Moore, Rossa Ryan booked, ran 4th and 7th on recent similar going — moderate form but likely to sit second or third and give a cleaner account of himself here stepping back to 5f on firmer ground.
runners_data.comment: Consistent between his two outings, posting similar figures each time and finishing eight lengths off in fourth at Goodwood second time out; speedily bred and suited to five furlongs, there could be a small step forward to come.

runners_data.name: Drum Major
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse carrying the cheekpieces flag, beaten in mid-to-rear on all three starts including twice on standard Windsor-style tracks; 40 days off and trainer Muir & Grassick out of form (0 from 10 in 14 days) compounds the concern.
runners_data.comment: Produced his most encouraging performance at five furlongs at Wolverhampton last time, beaten six lengths; a sprint pedigree is the main positive, and first-time cheekpieces today — he could find more when handicapping, but is yet to convince at this level.

runners_data.name: Divine Whisper
runners_data.note: George Boughey's hold-up filly was a solid 2nd on debut over this exact course, distance and going combination, giving her a meaningful form reference; Billy Loughnane takes the ride and 15 days between runs looks ideal — the standout closer in the race.
runners_data.comment: Closing all the way to the line at York on debut, beaten by a short-head in what looked a strong novice; sprint-bred and suited to good ground, she sets the obvious standard here — the trainer's recent record aside.

runners_data.name: Blondie Larry
runners_data.note: Lightly raced with just one run to her name, a 5th on soft ground for Jamie Osborne, so going to Good to Firm is an unknown; William Carver up, and her unknown style means she could slot anywhere — treat as a speculative unknown.
runners_data.comment: Showed fair enough on his debut at Nottingham, fading close home to finish three lengths off; a sprint pedigree suggests he will handle the distance, and a sound surface suits his action — there should be more to come.

runners_data.name: Trust Yourself
runners_data.note: James Tate's prominent runner has two runs on record, both 6f in Good going where he finished 10th and 11th — repeatedly well beaten, carries a fading-in-finish concern, and drop to 5f is unproven; hard to make a case at this stage of his career.
runners_data.comment: Nothing of note in two starts to date, with his Nottingham run particularly uninspiring; hard to fancy until he produces some evidence of ability, and he faces well-regarded rivals today.

runners_data.name: Wolf's Gallop
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's horse is the sole confirmed front-runner and has a STYLE_FIT flag suggesting he may not always perform as well when forced to lead — however he showed a 3rd on soft and 7th on Good, and uncontested today he is the key tactical figure regardless of absolute class.
runners_data.comment: Progressed between his first two starts, finishing two lengths off in third in a novice at Nottingham second time out; effective at five furlongs on a sound surface and with a touch more to offer, he looks a credible danger.

runners_data.name: Cash Flow Boy
runners_data.note: Debutant for Charlie Pike with a going record marked unknown; Thomas Greatrex rides and the trainer has posted 2 from 11 in the last 14 days — no form data to assess, so treat with full uncertainty on style and ability.
runners_data.comment: Ten Sovereigns gelding with a connection to Group-level black-type on the dam's side; making his debut here and likely to benefit from the run before showing his best.

runners_data.name: Nascent Star
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's lightly raced juvenile ran 4th on soft debut, stepping up to Good to Firm is an open question; Palmer's yard is in sharp form (6 from 53 in 14 days) and Ross Coakley is a capable conditional — the unknown upside here is real, even if the form book offers little.
runners_data.comment: Showed greenness on debut at Nottingham but closed steadily in the final stages to finish two lengths off in fourth; with a balanced pedigree offering both pace and stamina, he looks a well-regarded type who should improve with this experience behind him.

races.paceDynamic: Wolf's Gallop is the sole confirmed front-runner in this eight-runner 5f novice stakes on Good to Firm ground at Windsor, and with no genuine pace rival to push him, he should bowl along at a sustainable, controlled tempo from the outset. Seathegulls and Trust Yourself are the most likely to sit just behind in a prominent position, though Trust Yourself carries a fading flag and both have limited evidence of match-winning form. The hold-up contingent — Divine Whisper, Drum Major, and the unknowns Cash Flow Boy and Nascent Star — will need either a strong pace to chase or a late collapse from the leader to get into the race, neither of which looks guaranteed given Wolf's Gallop's uncontested status. This race shape strongly favours prominent-to-lead types who can travel smoothly just off the pace and quicken in the final furlong, with hold-up horses facing an uphill task against a well-set front-runner on a flat, fast track.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Controls Race
scenarios.trigger: If Wolf's Gallop leads uncontested and sets a steady-to-honest tempo, using his natural front-running style to boss the race throughout.
scenarios.body: If Wolf's Gallop leads uncontested and sets a steady-to-honest tempo, using his natural front-running style to boss the race throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Closer Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Wolf's Gallop sets a strong enough clip that a well-positioned prominent horse can reel him in inside the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If Wolf's Gallop sets a strong enough clip that a well-positioned prominent horse can reel him in inside the final furlong.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Lone Closer Finds Gap
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is strong enough to set the race up for a single hold-up horse who threads through late on the stands rail.
scenarios.body: If the pace is strong enough to set the race up for a single hold-up horse who threads through late on the stands rail.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Debutant Upsets Market
scenarios.trigger: If Cash Flow Boy or Nascent Star, racing first or second time out, produces an unexpectedly sharp piece of form to blind-side the experienced runners.
scenarios.body: If Cash Flow Boy or Nascent Star, racing first or second time out, produces an unexpectedly sharp piece of form to blind-side the experienced runners.

watchPoints.text: Watch Wolf's Gallop's jumping-out speed at the stalls — if he gains a clean break and immediately opens a length on the field, his uncontested lead is likely to be decisive on this fast ground.

Divine Whisper is the most interesting hold-up horse given her course-and-distance second on debut, but she needs the pace to be genuine; if Wolf's Gallop crawls, she may not get close enough to challenge and her chance evaporates.

Trust Yourself has been beaten 10th and 11th in both career starts — if Jack Mitchell pushes him forward given his prominent tag, he may use up energy that leads to another late fade and should be monitored early for signs of stopping.

Cash Flow Boy is a complete unknown on debut — watch the market move in the final 30 minutes; any support from 6/1 or shorter given his lack of form data could signal stable confidence worth tracking.

Drum Major runs in cheekpieces for the first time and has been off 40 days — headgear debutants in sprint novices occasionally produce sharp early pace or erratic behaviour, so note his early position to see if the gear change alters his hold-up tendencies.

races.name: Sri Lanka The Wonder Of Asia Handicap

runners_data.name: Angel Of Anfield
runners_data.note: In solid recent form with a 2212 sequence and a win and multiple placings on similar going; the sole natural leader here who should find the front without a fight, though a 50-day break and a trainer running at modest 2/13 over 14 days temper confidence slightly.
runners_data.comment: That reappearance at Ascot — where he trailed in well beaten — had the look of a fitness exercise; highly consistent through 2025 and suited to today's conditions over six furlongs, he should be a different proposition with that run under his belt.

runners_data.name: Combustion
runners_data.note: Has won twice on this trip on Standard ground but carries a poor record in similar going (0W0P in 2 runs on Good), and while genuinely prominent by nature, will need to push forward to express that style in a field stacked with pace types — the extra competition for position is a real concern.
runners_data.comment: Three wins in his last five starts all came on artificial surfaces, but his most recent turf run at Ascot over five furlongs was well short of his best; today's six furlongs is a better fit, though he still has something to prove on grass.

runners_data.name: Marcellinus
runners_data.note: Consistent 3yo with a win and four places in last six, all on Good or Good-type ground at six furlongs, making him the standout profile fit for the dominant scenario; Tom Dascombe has 0 wins from 13 runners in the past fortnight, worth noting.
runners_data.comment: Beaten by a nose off a lower mark last time in a performance that suggested he is on an upward curve; handles six furlongs on a range of going, and with that close effort under his belt, a 3lb rise need not be prohibitive.

runners_data.name: Alasrae
runners_data.note: Has won and placed on similar going at this trip and distance, though his recent sequence includes a 7th on Good and he carries headgear (t); Billy Loughnane's booking adds a positive angle for a George Boughey yard that has been quiet recently.
runners_data.comment: Third at two lengths off an unchanged mark last time out, performing to his usual level; consistent throughout and at home over today's distance and going, though the trainer's poor recent record and first-time tongue-tie add an element of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Betsen
runners_data.note: A 7lb claimer takes the ride and this hold-up specialist has poor recent form — 8th, 9th, 13th in last three, including twice on Good ground at this distance; Tony Carroll's yard is active but this profile needs more pace ahead of it than may materialise.
runners_data.comment: Holds an unchanged official mark after finishing three-and-a-quarter lengths off the winner last time on a 4lb rise; handles any ground over today's trip but the handicapper looks to have him on a slightly tight rating at present.

runners_data.name: Desert Cop
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up type with 14 runs on Good going making him experienced in these conditions, but the flat Windsor straight offers limited scope for a late swoop and three placings without a win in 14 similar-going starts tells its own story; ran just 5 days ago.
runners_data.comment: First-time cheekpieces today as connections look for more; losing ground after a tardy start when tried at five furlongs at this course last time, he is better suited to today's extra distance on a sound surface, though questions about his attitude persist.

runners_data.name: Star Chorus
runners_data.note: Won on Standard ground at six furlongs and has placed at five; hold-up style noted (hg:h), but only 4 runs from 15 on similar going make the Good to Firm conditions a mild concern despite the headgear suggesting trainer intent.
runners_data.comment: Dropped away tamely at Epsom last time but the going was likely against him on that occasion; wearing a hood for the first time on quicker ground that plays to his strengths, a recovery is within reach if the conditions help.

runners_data.name: Kiniro
runners_data.note: A true hold-up type whose recent Good-ground form reads 11th and 8th; the redistribution to midfield reflects field congestion at the rear, not an upgrade in style, and a 7lb claimer in the saddle adds to the risk against stronger-profile rivals.
runners_data.comment: Battled tenaciously when second at Newbury last time, two lengths off at this level on the same official mark; handled the trip and going well enough, and his attitude is hard to fault, though the handicapper looks to have him rated rather tightly.

runners_data.name: An Outlaw's Grace
runners_data.note: Richard Hannon yard is active (8/53 in 14 days) and this horse won on Good ground at the trip in its history, but recent form reads 7-7-6-2-0 and the hold-up style is squeezed to midfield by sheer weight of closers in this field — hard to fancy at face value.
runners_data.comment: Dropped well out of contention at York most recently, with that race possibly arriving too quickly; first-time cheekpieces as connections try to unlock more, but a winless record and an inconsistent profile make him hard to trust at this level.

runners_data.name: Dublin Bay
runners_data.note: The most credible genuine hold-up runner in the field with two wins at seven furlongs on Standard; dropping back to six on Good to Firm is a slight query, but Robert Havlin's booking and a yard firing at 2/21 keep him interesting if pace collapses.
runners_data.comment: Came home seven lengths clear at Wolverhampton last time when back at seven furlongs — a performance that flatters his current mark if he can reproduce that level; keen to make his own running, he is versatile enough for today's shorter distance, though the drop back in trip is the main query.

runners_data.name: Jax Edge
runners_data.note: Won most recently on Good at six furlongs and has a solid record in similar conditions (2W5P in 9 tries); a prominent type who should get his position on a straight track, making him a natural fit for the dominant scenario if he can settle cleanly.
runners_data.comment: Suited to course and conditions and landed a Bath handicap by two lengths last time off a lower mark; the six-pound rise in the weights looks the significant obstacle now, though a trainer in decent form provides some support.

runners_data.name: Supreme King
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a win on Soft and modest records on Standard; Good to Firm conditions are a clear unknown (0W0P in sole similar-going start) and the prominent tag works in his favour tactically, but Rossa Ryan will need to slot him into position quickly in a busy pace scenario.
runners_data.comment: Returned to his best at Salisbury last time, landing a handicap by a neck off a marginally lower mark; consistent across conditions and effective over today's distances, he rates as a genuine threat from a mark just 2lb higher.

races.paceDynamic: Angel Of Anfield is the one confirmed front-runner here, and on Good to Firm ground over Windsor's straight six furlongs she should find a comfortable, uncontested lead with no genuine pace rival willing to push her hard from the gates. Marcellinus, Alasrae, Jax Edge, and Supreme King all carry prominent tags but with the field stacked with pace types, Combustion — a natural prominent racer — is the most likely of the redistributed horses to push forward and challenge Angel Of Anfield for early position, potentially creating slightly more pressure than the headline pace map suggests. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred berth; Marcellinus and Alasrae, with strong recent course-appropriate form, are best placed to actually hold prominent ground. The sustained, manageable tempo set by Angel Of Anfield on fast ground over a flat six furlongs strongly favours horses racing prominently in the first three or four, with closers — particularly true hold-up types — facing an uphill task to reel in a well-set leader before the line.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Of Anfield secures an uncontested or lightly-pressed lead and the prominent horses settle in behind without disruption.
scenarios.body: If Angel Of Anfield secures an uncontested or lightly-pressed lead and the prominent horses settle in behind without disruption.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Contested, Strong Stayer
scenarios.trigger: If Combustion pushes forward early and genuinely tests Angel Of Anfield, creating a faster-than-expected pace that sets up a late challenge.
scenarios.body: If Combustion pushes forward early and genuinely tests Angel Of Anfield, creating a faster-than-expected pace that sets up a late challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely hot early and the prominent brigade ties itself up, allowing a well-placed hold-up runner to land a late blow.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely hot early and the prominent brigade ties itself up, allowing a well-placed hold-up runner to land a late blow.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Front Runner Bowls Up
scenarios.trigger: If Angel Of Anfield is entirely untroubled and the prominent horses fail to close the gap through the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: If Angel Of Anfield is entirely untroubled and the prominent horses fail to close the gap through the final two furlongs.

watchPoints.text: Combustion has the natural instinct to race prominently and if Joey Haynes sends him forward early, he could contest Angel Of Anfield's lead and turn this into a truly-run six furlongs — transforming the pace shape significantly.

The prominent group — Marcellinus, Alasrae, Jax Edge, and Supreme King — are all chasing the same early positions on a straight track, and crowding or interference off the gates could disrupt several of their chances simultaneously.

Dublin Bay drops from seven furlongs to six furlongs on faster ground than most of his wins; if he cannot produce his usual hold-up finish at the shorter trip, his otherwise credible profile is undermined.

Good to Firm ground is confirmed for this race despite the headline going listed as Good — all horses should be assessed against their fast-ground records, and Supreme King (0W0P on similar) and Star Chorus (limited fast-ground exposure) face a genuine surface question.

races.name: Sporting Times Sri Lanka Handicap

runners_data.name: Guernsey Lady
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan partners this David Evans 3yo who has placed placed at this trip on soft-side ground, but her natural style is genuine hold-up and she arrives 23 days fresh; she tends to be seen to best effect when a true pace softens the field up ahead of her, though she is effectively squeezed into a midfield slot by the volume of hold-up types in this field.|
runners_data.comment: Two lengths off the winner at Ffos Las last time on the same official mark, though that effort suggested she might prefer a slightly stiffer test than five furlongs; today's six furlongs on fast ground is closer to her ideal, and the mark remains competitive.

runners_data.name: Eightthreeone
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton's 3yo won over 6f at Sandown and runs on ground she handles, but her customary race-from-the-front approach is being displaced by the presence of Quantum Power — she'll likely find herself tracking rather than leading, which partially compromises a profile built on prominent racing.|
runners_data.comment: A consistent performer who finished a length and a half behind in second last time on an unchanged mark; effective at today's distances on a range of going, though his action ideally suits softer conditions than he is likely to encounter today.

runners_data.name: Adalida
runners_data.note: Stuart Williams sends out this 3yo who won over 5f on good ground at this trip, a positive form line, but a trainer strike rate of 0/19 over 14 days tempers enthusiasm; she'll be pushed further back than her natural style demands by the stronger pace presence of Quantum Power, diluting her best chance.|
runners_data.comment: Her most recent run was effectively ended by a sluggish start, losing ground at the off before being beaten close to ten lengths; a pound lower in the weights today, and a clean break could see her bounce back to something like her winning form.

runners_data.name: Quantum Power
runners_data.note: Tom Clover's Billy Loughnane-ridden 3yo won over this exact 5f Good trip last time and is the only confirmed front-runner in the field — he wears a visor, arrives just 7 days on from his last run which is worth monitoring for freshness, and the uncontested lead on a flat, fast Windsor straight suits his profile ideally.|
runners_data.comment: Took a handicap at Newmarket by a length and a half last time; a first-time visor goes on today, and effective on any ground over five or six furlongs and well suited to today's conditions, he should remain competitive despite a 5lb rise.

runners_data.name: Alkuwarrior
runners_data.note: Gina Mangan takes the ride on this Christopher Mason 3yo who won over 5f on soft ground last time; he wears a hood and his hold-up style is genuine, meaning he needs the pace to be truly strong before his late run can be effective — his sole win came on soft, and the good-to-firm surface here is a query.|
runners_data.comment: Landed a Ffos Las handicap by two lengths last time; now 7lb higher, the question is whether he can repeat that form, though first-time cheekpieces and a trainer in good form provide some encouragement.

runners_data.name: Angel Numbers
runners_data.note: Pierre-Louis Jamin rides this Dr Newland & Insole 3yo who has twice placed over 5f, including a second on firm ground, and wears a tongue tie; he races from hold-up and his best efforts have come when the gallop has been honest, but no wins from 12 runs on similar going is a concern.|
runners_data.comment: Her York run — where she was badly positioned throughout and beaten eight lengths — can be excused by a difficult draw; tongue-tie added for the first time today, though the trainer has yet to strike in recent starts and her consistency has been mixed.

runners_data.name: Dark Alley
runners_data.note: Thomas Greatrex rides the Warren Greatrex-trained 3yo who placed over 5f on good ground and won over 6f on firm — course-form profile suits this race shape well and his prominent, stalking style is perfectly suited to tracking Quantum Power in a race with just one natural front-runner.|
runners_data.comment: Ridden prominently at Goodwood on his return to action, going on to finish three lengths off on a mark just above today's; suited to fast ground and today's distances, with improvement expected as he sharpens up from that seasonal debut.

runners_data.name: Control Room
runners_data.note: Seamus Cronin (5lb claim) partners Robert Cowell's 3yo who won over 5f on soft and placed over 6f on good — the step up in going firmness is the key query, with only one run on similar ground in his last five; from a prominent position he could challenge late, but the jockey claim is a double-edged advantage given the greenness of the booking.|
runners_data.comment: Only a head away on her handicap debut at Bath, performing to expectation on a mark 3lb below today's; effective on a range of going, she could improve further with that experience behind her, though our figures put her towards the foot of the field.

races.paceDynamic: Quantum Power is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with only one horse intent on leading, will dictate from the gates at a controlled but honest gallop on this Good to Firm Windsor 5f straight. Dark Alley and Control Room are the genuine prominent horses who should secure the positions directly behind Quantum Power, with Eightthreeone and Adalida — both natural prominent types — likely to find themselves a touch further back than they'd prefer given the competition for early position. The field holds more prominent and near-prominent types than can all get their natural spot: Eightthreeone and Adalida are most likely to be squeezed out of the front rank, while Guernsey Lady, mapped to midfield, is a true hold-up horse who may get a cleaner passage than her rivals expect. With one uncontested front-runner setting a sustainable pace on a flat, fast-running straight course, this race shape strongly favours horses racing prominently just off the leader — those who can track Quantum Power comfortably and have the finishing kick to collared him in the final furlong — rather than those relying on a late, deep-closing run.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Quantum Power Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Quantum Power leads uncontested and sets a measured but fair pace that keeps closers honest throughout.
scenarios.body: If Quantum Power leads uncontested and sets a measured but fair pace that keeps closers honest throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Trackers Overhaul Leader
scenarios.trigger: If Quantum Power's lead is pegged back in the final furlong by well-placed prominent horses who have been travelling within themselves.
scenarios.body: If Quantum Power's lead is pegged back in the final furlong by well-placed prominent horses who have been travelling within themselves.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Midfield Sweeps
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is faster than expected, burning out Quantum Power early and opening the race up for horses with a mid-race sustained run.
scenarios.body: If the pace is faster than expected, burning out Quantum Power early and opening the race up for horses with a mid-race sustained run.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops Late
scenarios.trigger: If the early gallop is genuinely strong and the prominent brigade over-race, leaving a pocket for a pure closer to sprint through.
scenarios.body: If the early gallop is genuinely strong and the prominent brigade over-race, leaving a pocket for a pure closer to sprint through.

watchPoints.text: Quantum Power (Loughnane) — if he jumps cleanly and takes an uncontested lead, watch whether any rival seriously tries to pressurise him early, as a truly unchallenged Quantum Power is the defining shape of this race.

Eightthreeone and Adalida — both natural prominent horses who cannot get their favoured position in this field; watch for them to be restless or keen early as they are forced to settle for a deeper pitch than their style demands.

Alkuwarrior — the hood is on and this horse showed ability on soft ground, but a step to good-to-firm over 5f is an unresolved going question; watch the market move for a signal on how connections regard the conditions.

Control Room (Cronin 5) — Robert Cowell is a shrewd handler of sprinters and the apprentice claim could exploit a light weight, but watch whether Control Room travels smoothly off Quantum Power's pace — if he's hard-ridden early the claim becomes a liability rather than an asset.

Dark Alley — 35 days since his last run and no win on good ground in recent starts, but his placings in similar conditions and his prominent style make him the most tactically well-placed of the challengers; watch where Thomas Greatrex slots him at the break.

races.name: Sporting Times Sri Lanka British Stallion Studs EBF Novice Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Peace And Quiet
runners_data.comment: Held up in a novice here last time and threw his chance away by failing to settle; the extra distance may prove an advantage if he can control his enthusiasm, though this remains a big step up in class.

runners_data.name: Ruler Of Time
runners_data.comment: Beaten two lengths into second in a novice at Doncaster last time, consistent form on going that suits him; yet to score despite running to his level in recent starts, and our top figure makes him the one to beat here.

runners_data.name: Lunella
runners_data.comment: Highly bought Lope Y Fernandez filly with quality stamina on both sides of the pedigree — a close relative is a high-class stayer and the dam was useful over twelve furlongs; wears a hood first time and likely needs the experience, but the breeding is hard to ignore.

runners_data.name: Gonna Fly
runners_data.comment: That last run — where he was visibly unsettled in the preliminaries and raced far too freely — can be put firmly to one side; he won impressively on debut and has the ability to be competitive here if he travels more kindly.

races.name: Sri Lanka Paradise Island Handicap (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Claymore
runners_data.note: Seven-year-old who switches to the front-running role here under Billy Loughnane for Jane Chapple-Hyam; recent form reads poorly but most of those runs came over shorter trips and he is rated slightly out of role as a natural prominent type taking the lead by default — treat with tempered optimism rather than confidence.
runners_data.comment: Former Group-level winner stepping back into handicap company; suited by today's trip and going, he shaped with some credit at Carlisle last time, though six lengths adrift and well short of his peak form.

runners_data.name: King's Code
runners_data.note: David Evans runner whose recent similar-going record of just one place from 15 runs is deeply concerning, and last-time form of 0-0-0 makes him very hard to support; hold-up style is genuine but he needs a faster pace than this race is likely to generate to produce his best.
runners_data.comment: Entitled to a better showing than his Epsom effort, where he dropped away tamely; now fitted with blinkers for the first time and carrying a mark a shade below his last successful level, he handles this trip and conditions and has it all to prove.

runners_data.name: Wisper
runners_data.note: Alan King's eight-year-old is a true hold-up horse in the fullest sense, and his last win came at this trip and going only 40 days ago — the redistribution to a midfield slot on the map understates how far back he will likely race; the structural problem is that a single unforced front-runner rarely generates enough pace to bring hold-up horses into it at Windsor.
runners_data.comment: Successful in this race last year and back to her best last time out, landing a course-and-distance handicap with something in hand off a mark 3lb lower than today's; handles any ground over this trip and clearly thrives here — the trainer's recent record is the only caveat.

runners_data.name: Pride Of Donegal
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's four-year-old won twice at this trip on Standard going and is visor-equipped, which can sharpen his early behaviour; he is a natural front-runner who will find himself in a more congested mid-pack than ideal given the number of prominent types in this field, and his similar-going record (0 wins, 1 place from 14 runs on Good) is a legitimate concern.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Wolverhampton handicap convincingly three starts back but all his best form has come on artificial surfaces, which is a concern on turf today; first-time visor is interesting but a dip in form last time makes him hard to place with confidence.

runners_data.name: Thinthread
runners_data.note: Andre Fabre's three-year-old arrives on a 263-day absence and racing at a new track for the first time, which are both significant unknowns; a natural prominent type who will struggle to hold that position against more experienced rivals, and the extended layoff combined with a trainer who has sent just 0 from 6 in the last 14 days makes this a significant risk.
runners_data.comment: Off the track since October, he faces a tough ask on his stable debut after such a lengthy absence; handles the trip on a sound surface and his French form is respectable, but freshness is likely to count against him here.

runners_data.name: Spioradalta
runners_data.note: Mark Walford's six-year-old is fresh off a win just 15 days ago and has won four of his last 11 on Good ground, including two at this trip — the prominent style fits the race shape perfectly and Jack Garritty maintains the partnership; the key query is whether a quick turnaround blunts his finish.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Ripon handicap by a length two starts back and handles any ground over this kind of trip; up 3lb and facing stiffer company, though his last run may have been compromised by pulling too hard, which tempers enthusiasm somewhat.

runners_data.name: Majestic
runners_data.note: Rose Dawes takes the ride on Jack Channon's eight-year-old, who has just one win from 10 similar-going runs and whose recent form includes a 19th on Heavy and a 7th on Good — the hold-up style is genuine and his best effort last time (4th over 11f Good) is not without merit, but he needs more pace than this race will likely provide.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Hamilton on his latest start, an improvement on earlier 2026 efforts, though seven lengths off the pace and on a mark that remains above what his current form has merited; at home over the trip and on this going.

runners_data.name: Fireblade
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's five-year-old has spent most of his career over far longer trips (16-18f) and has won at those extreme distances on Good ground; dropping back to 1m3½f could be a shorter-than-ideal trip, but his prominent style and fresh legs after 67 days off give him residual interest if he handles the reduction in distance.
runners_data.comment: Held his form with credit when fourth at Pontefract despite that run being over a shorter trip than ideal; stepping out to a more appropriate distance is a clear plus, and he travels well on a sound surface.

races.paceDynamic: Claymore is the one confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine challenger for the lead, will set a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m3½f Windsor trip on Good to Firm ground — the pace will be honest but measured, with no pressure applied early. Spioradalta and Fireblade are genuine prominent types who should sit just behind Claymore in the first two or three positions, creating a compact early order with limited gaps. The field contains more pace-oriented horses than the map can cleanly place — Pride Of Donegal and Thinthread are natural prominent racers who will be shuffled back against their instincts, while Wisper is a genuine hold-up type similarly displaced — meaning the early order may be slightly more congested than the simple map implies. A single uncontested leader setting a fair but unforced pace on a flat, fast surface over an extended trip strongly favours prominent and pace-pressing profiles who can travel close to the action without burning energy, rather than hold-up horses who must find a gap in a race unlikely to truly fall apart.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Pace, Pressers Win
scenarios.trigger: If Claymore dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and Spioradalta or Fireblade sit within striking range throughout.
scenarios.body: If Claymore dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and Spioradalta or Fireblade sit within striking range throughout.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Front Runner Outstays Field
scenarios.trigger: If Claymore rolls along at a pace his rivals underestimate and kicks clear before the field can organise a serious challenge.
scenarios.body: If Claymore rolls along at a pace his rivals underestimate and kicks clear before the field can organise a serious challenge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Collide Late
scenarios.trigger: If Pride Of Donegal and Thinthread push forward from their mapped positions to reclaim their natural prominent berths, creating a fractionally stronger pace.
scenarios.body: If Pride Of Donegal and Thinthread push forward from their mapped positions to reclaim their natural prominent berths, creating a fractionally stronger pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closers Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is set fast enough through the final mile to compromise those prominent horses who have expended energy, leaving a late window for hold-up runners.
scenarios.body: If the pace is set fast enough through the final mile to compromise those prominent horses who have expended energy, leaving a late window for hold-up runners.

watchPoints.text: Thinthread has been absent 263 days — watch the market closely pre-race; if supported significantly it suggests an Fabre stable move, but an unconsidered drifter should be sidelined immediately given the cold trainer stats and the step into a new environment.

Pride Of Donegal's position in the first furlong will be crucial — if he successfully pushes forward to reclaim his natural prominent pitch rather than settling mid-pack, he becomes a materially bigger danger in Scenario C; watch where he travels in the opening two furlongs.

Spioradalta is on a quick 15-day turnaround following a winning run — watch his price movement; if connections are confident the bounce risk is low he could be significantly shorter, but any significant drifting from an expected SP may signal a tired horse.

Claymore's early fractions will define the entire race — if he bowls along in front uncontested without Spioradalta or Fireblade applying any pressure, the solo-leader scenario (Scenario B) becomes appreciably more live than the 18% base probability suggests.

Wisper's draw and how quickly Rossa Ryan settles him will indicate whether a hold-up run is even viable — if he is forced wider or catches traffic early on this tight Windsor circuit, his chance of threading through in time is almost nil.

races.name: Visit Sri Lanka Fillies' Handicap

runners_data.name: Hot Silk
runners_data.note: A hold-up filly for James Fanshawe who steps up significantly in trip to 1m3½f for the first time; returning after 47 days off, her three career runs have all come at shorter on soft or standard ground, so both the extra distance and the faster surface represent unknowns that narrow her ceiling here.
runners_data.comment: Fourth at Wolverhampton most recently, well beaten but that performance probably reflected her current level; handles softer ground well, but yet to score in her last three starts and faces a step up in class here.

runners_data.name: Kindly Queen
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has solid placed form over 10-12f on good and soft ground and holds obvious form credentials, having finished second over this sort of trip; a genuine hold-up operator by nature, she will find the race shape difficult to exploit with Glenna likely to crawl, and the pace is unlikely to force the searching finish she needs to peel off her rivals.
runners_data.comment: Wore herself out in front at Newbury last time, but connections try first-time cheekpieces today and this stable has a strong record in this race; effective over today's trip and going, she may just benefit from being allowed to stride clear without pressure early to find her rhythm and show her best.

runners_data.name: Mohaab
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on soft for William Muir & Chris Grassick and carries fair form over a mile and a quarter; a true hold-up horse at heart, Billy Loughnane will find her travelling through mid-to-rear territory in a race where the pace is set to be tepid, and her record on good-to-firm going is sparse — four runs in similar conditions produced no wins or places.
runners_data.comment: Landed a Nottingham handicap by five lengths two starts back off a lower mark; a step up in trip may bring out more, but fast ground appeared to limit her last time out, which makes today's conditions a reservation.

runners_data.name: Glenna
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's filly is the sole pace influence in the race and can dictate completely from the front, with Pierre-Louis Jamin able to control every variable; her second over 12f on soft at Kempton is the best form pointer for this trip, though she has yet to win, and the key question is whether a steady pace suits her enough to maintain the advantage to the line.
runners_data.comment: Placed at Newbury in a stronger contest last time, keeping on to finish four lengths off; handles twelve furlongs on any ground and has been a consistent presence in recent starts — she looks the one to beat on form here.

runners_data.name: Ticker Tape
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden send out this hold-up filly after 39 days off; her recent third over 8f at Newmarket on standard was encouraging, and the step up to 1m3½f on good-to-firm is an open question, but Robert Havlin may elect to travel handy rather than deep given the likely lack of gallop, which could make her style more relevant here than her mapping suggests.
runners_data.comment: Beaten nine lengths at Newcastle last time over an extended distance where stamina may have been stretched; all her form to date has come on artificial surfaces, though fast ground here should suit her action and the trainer is in good shape — the trip remains a genuine concern.

races.paceDynamic: Glenna is the sole confirmed front runner in this five-runner fillies' handicap over 1m3½f at Windsor on good-to-firm ground, and with no genuine challenger for the lead, Pierre-Louis Jamin can dictate an entirely uncontested, controlled gallop from the front. That scenario creates a sustainable, even tempo which will not significantly drain Glenna's reserves, meaning the race is unlikely to turn into the searching test of stamina that would otherwise drag a front runner back. The field holds more hold-up types than the race shape can accommodate at the rear — Kindly Queen and Mohaab are genuine hold-up horses in form terms but are mapped to midfield because the race cannot place them all at the back, and their ability to travel in their natural position behind a crawling pace is genuinely constrained. This shape strongly favours the leader or any horse handy enough to track Glenna on her own terms, as the honest fractions will never build sufficient pressure to dislodge a horse who can dictate and quicken.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Glenna Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Glenna bowls along uncontested at a controlled pace and Jamin preserves her energy through the long Windsor straight.
scenarios.body: If Glenna bowls along uncontested at a controlled pace and Jamin preserves her energy through the long Windsor straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a prominent or mid-division horse travels smoothly just behind Glenna and produces a superior late kick when the tempo lifts.
scenarios.body: If a prominent or mid-division horse travels smoothly just behind Glenna and produces a superior late kick when the tempo lifts.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Finish Through
scenarios.trigger: If Glenna sets a surprisingly brisk pace from the front and the hold-up horses are able to find clear daylight and run on late.
scenarios.body: If Glenna sets a surprisingly brisk pace from the front and the hold-up horses are able to find clear daylight and run on late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Muddled Tactical Scramble
scenarios.trigger: If Glenna is checked or faces early pressure disrupting her rhythm, causing a bunched and unpredictable finish.
scenarios.body: If Glenna is checked or faces early pressure disrupting her rhythm, causing a bunched and unpredictable finish.

watchPoints.text: Glenna's ability to control the pace completely is the single most consequential factor — if Jamin elects to go steady and no rival has the tactical speed to challenge for the lead, this race effectively becomes hers to lose.

Kindly Queen and Mohaab are both natural hold-up horses whose optimum scenario — a strongly-run race where they can close through a tiring field — is the least likely outcome given the pace map; monitor market confidence, as significant support for either would suggest connections expect more tempo than the shape implies.

Ticker Tape is returning after 39 days and races over a trip longer than she has previously tackled; if she travels fluently behind Glenna and handles the extra distance, her Gosden handler and Havlin combo could be significant at a likely bigger price.

Hot Silk has no form on fast ground and tackles a career-longest trip on just her fourth start after a 47-day absence; her chance is most dependent on the unknown quantities of trip and going combining favourably, which makes her difficult to assess with confidence.
